To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) COVID-19 is an intergroup challenge; (2) intergroup relations are a critical factor in the social psychology of the pandemic; (3) the intergroup dimension of the pandemic is likely to exacerbate intergroup tensions and conflict; (4) intergroup tensions and conflicts can be managed by the leadership and social cohesion; (5) social identity and social cohesion can be used as a tool to manage intergroup tensions and intergroup conflicts.
social identity processes are central to understanding and managing the COVID 19 pandemic, both at the level of individual behavior and at the level of policy and social cohesion.

the intergroup dimension of the COVID pandemic can be understood as a process of social identity uncertainty, which has implications for social cohesion and social fragmentation, and can be managed by leaders who can provide a sense of shared identity and common fate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the intergroup and intragroup dynamics of the COVID 19 pandemic.
the social identity dynamics of the pandemic and how they can help us better understand, manage, and resolve social and intergroup conflict.

how people perceive and respond to the pandemic in terms of their own social identity, and how this is shaped by their social group membership and intergroup relations, as well as by the leadership and social cohesion of their group.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the social psychological challenge is to sustain the super-ordinate objective of surviving, and recovering from, the pandemic through mutual effort.
COVID 19 is an unprecedented challenge that has the potential to exacerbate intergroup tensions and divisions.

COVID 19 is not just a personal health issue, nor a government policy problem, it is also a social identity challenge that can lead to social fragmentation and unity, and thus needs a more integrated social psychological and policy response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pandemic is a social and psychological challenge for which we need to understand the social identity dynamics of the pandemic to manage and resolve them.
social identities are a powerful force in the pandemic.
we have a better understanding of how social identity and social categorization processes are related to the social and psychological challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pandemic is not only an individual challenge, but a social challenge that requires intergroup understanding, empathy, and coordination.
social identity and group processes are central to understanding how to manage and resolve COVID 19.
social identity theory can provide a useful framework for understanding and managing intergroup and intragroup dynamics in the pandemic, and for the long term recovery from it.
